newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London ended lower in technical trading. March lost $0.10 to close at $305.10. Traders said technically the market is oversold and a bounce from the lows is imminent. However, current fundamentals suggest that after a period of consolidation prices could drift lower.

Symptomatic is an announcement by senior Polish sugar officials who said that Poland may export some 400,000 tonnes of white sugar without subsidies in 1997 as a successful beet campaign is likely to result in record sugar output of 2.1 million tonnes in 1996/97.

However, it remains to be seen whether the country can get rid of the total surplus. Poland failed to export all of its subsidised quota of about 120,000 tonnes this year. However, cross-border shoppers, especially from CIS states, reportedly bought significant amounts of sugar retail.
UNITED KINGDOM - Sugar consumption in June 1996 amounted to 208,913 tonnes, raw value, sharply down from May's 231,848 tonnes and 212,500 tonnes consumed in June 1995.

This brought cumulative consumption in the first three quarters of 1995/96 (October/June) up to 1.71 million tonnes, 3.7 per cent down on the 1.78 million tonnes consumed in the like period the previous year. Total consumption 1994/95 amounted to 2.38 million tonnes against 2.43 million tonnes in 1993/94.

SOUTH AFRICA - Based on latest campaign data, the South African sugar industry expects total sugar production in 1996/97 (May/April) to reach 2.35 million tonnes, tel quel, sharply up on the 1995/96 result of 1.67 million tonnes.

Molasses output is expected to hit 870,000 tonnes against 743,000 tonnes in 1995/95. According to industry sources, sugar consumption is also forecast to rise to 1.30 million tonnes up from 1.28 million tonnes in 1995/96 and 1.24 million tonnes in 1994/95.

BARBADOS - The sugar industry in Barbados expects production to recover further in 1997 with overall output estimated at 62,000 tonnes, raw value, up from 59,000 tonnes in 1996 and 55,000 tonnes in 1995.
As domestic consumption is expected to hold steady at around 15,000 tonnes the country will be able to meet all its export obligations.
